answer: A randomized retrospective audit lottery makes bulk forgery uneconomic. New identities start probationary: the protocol randomly samples a fraction each round for deep review of their work history, endorsements, and transaction links, with staked auditors paid from a bounty pool. A fake that slips through ordinary checks still faces this later draw, like pigment that cannot wander unnoticed across a tundra: once one forgery is caught, its endorsers are slashed and linked identities revoked, so an attacker must make every fake audit-proof, multiplying cost per identity instead of amortizing it.
